error.message: Rider "rider" has a targetHas on "any-crit". Only every-hit and first-hit riders are gated on a condition of the target.
"rider" has a targetHas that is not a non-empty list of condition names.
Rider "rider" has a targetHas and watches the rider "r0". A gated rider is folded into attack draws: watch the attacks directly.
Rider "rider" has a targetHas and is named by another entry. A gated rider is folded into its attacks' draws and can be neither.

Condition "g" has a targetHas on "first-hit". Only every-hit, any-crit and any-miss conditions are gated on a condition of the target: a once-per-turn gate would need a first that counts only open ones.
Rider "cx" has a payload per attack on "any-miss". Only first-hit, every-hit and any-crit riders take one.
Condition "cnd" names a rider beside other entries in "of"; a condition fires where one rider landed, or on its rows.
Condition "cnd" counts "sneak" landing on "nowhere", which is not in this turn.
Condition "cnd" has "where" for "b", which is not the rider in its "of".
Rider "adept" has "where" for "smite", which is not a partner in its "of".
Rider "adept" lands alongside a partner, so it lands once: use first-hit.
Rider "third" lands alongside "adept", which itself lands alongside a partner; name a rider that lands on its own.
Rider "adept" lands alongside "smite", so it is dealt with that rider's landing and cannot roll an attack of its own. Give it damage, or watch the attacks directly.
Rider "a" joins "attack 1", but joins needs a source that pools the rider's dice via under(context).joined; this row's source does not.
Rider "a" joins "attack 2", which it does not watch: a rider's dice join a row only where it can land.
Rider "a" joins rows but lands on anything: a miss has no roll to join.
"r1" triggers on "fb", which has no hit/crit outcomes. It is a save: a rider can watch a save row by declaring `landing` ("fail" or "damage").
Rider "nf" declares a landing on "not-fired", which watches a rider, not attacks. A landing says how to read a save among attack sources.
Attack "w" happens after "sneak", a rider that rolls its own attack. Only a rider that deals damage can gate an attack.
Attack "w" happens after "sneak", a rider that may not happen (happens 0.5). Its coin would have to be shared by the rider's damage and the gated attack, which a gate cannot do.
Attack "w" happens after "nf", a not-fired rider. Only a rider that reads attacks can gate an attack.
Attack "w" happens after rider "sneak", which watches "b", an attack that does not come before it.
"a" is read by a condition that needs fire damage dealt, but its source cannot say the odds it deals it (ContextualSource.dealt).
A turn may name one damage type a landing must deal; this one names fire, cold.
Condition "cnd" needs fire damage dealt, which only a hit or crit of an attack row can say.
Condition "st" starts on "nobody", which no attack is aimed at. Name "target" or an attack's target.
Condition "st" is in force from the start, so nothing tries it: it takes no "chance".
Condition "cnd" needs a chance in [0, 1], got 1.5.
Condition "cnd" names a target, which only a "start" condition takes: the others are on the creature of the row that lands them.
Condition "cnd" has onSave grants but no save or chance: there is no other branch to apply them on.
Substitutes "kh1" and "kh2" both watch "a". One transform per source: two would apply to the same payload.
Substitutes "conv" and "rr" both watch "a". A hit conversion and a reroll would both rewrite the same miss.
Substitutes "rr" and "conv" both watch "a". A hit conversion and a reroll would both rewrite the same miss.
Substitute "kh" spends below a threshold, which cannot be priced beside a first-miss reroll: a reroll turns a miss into a landing the look-ahead does not see. Use the "always" policy.
Substitute "conv" converts the first miss, which takes no policy.
Substitute "kh" asks for the optimal policy, which this release does not support.
"conv" triggers on "f", which has no hit/crit outcomes.
Substitute "conv" converts a miss of "rr", an any-miss reroll that resolves after every declared attack. Use onFirstMiss, which resolves right after the miss.
Substitute "conv" converts a miss of "a", which rider "rr" rerolls first. Convert the rider's reroll instead: leave "a" out of `of`.
"kh" watches "cnd", a condition. A condition changes later attack rolls; it rolls no attack to watch.
Substitute "kh" spends below a threshold, but "a" supplies its own reroll (rerolledUnder), which has no base payload to compare. Drop the policy.

"after" watches "fl", a list of several attacks. A list rider resolves as one payload, not as attacks that each land, so it cannot be watched. Declare each attack as its own rider with its own id, and name those.
